title: Local Entropy Search over Descent Sequences for Bayesian Optimization
claim: Uncertainty about an objective induces a distribution over local-optimizer trajectories and optima, which collapses toward the deterministic case as data arrives.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, shared legend below, deterministic→prior→posterior progression
description: Three side-by-side 1-D function plots share a horizontal x axis and a dashed vertical line marking the starting point x0. Left, 'Deterministic': a single black curve with an orange descent path running downhill from x0 to a local minimum, marked by an orange tick on the bottom axis. Middle, 'Prior': a blue shaded GP confidence band with many dotted black GP sample curves. Orange descent sequences fan out from x0 across the samples, and orange ticks along the bottom show widely spread local optima. Right, 'Posterior': the band is pinched around two starred observed points, and a bold dashed posterior mean passes through them. Orange descent paths and optimum ticks are now tightly clustered. A legend below lists GP samples, local optima, descent sequences and x0.
caption: Distribution over Descent Sequences: Left: Local optimization on the unknown objective function. Middle: The prior over the objective function induces a belief over descent sequences. Right: After sampling data points the distributions over descent sequences and local optimum approach the deterministic ones. In LES the next query minimizes the entropy of the descent sequences.
abstract: Searching large and complex design spaces for a global optimum can be infeasible and unnecessary. A practical alternative is to iteratively refine the neighborhood of an initial design using local optimization methods such as gradient descent. We propose local entropy search (LES), a Bayesian optimization paradigm that explicitly targets the solutions reachable by the descent sequences of iterative optimizers. The algorithm propagates the posterior belief over the objective through the optimizer, resulting in a probability distribution over descent sequences. It then selects the next evaluation by maximizing mutual information with that distribution, using a combination of analytic entropy calculations and Monte-Carlo sampling of descent sequences. Empirical results on high-complexity synthetic objectives and benchmark problems show that LES achieves strong sample efficiency compared to existing local and global Bayesian optimization methods.
